Add `process.flags` for declarative command-line flag generation using `lib.cli.toCommandLine`, with per-flag ordering via valueMeta.
Add `process.flagFormat` to control flag rendering.
Add `process.env` for environment variables.

Used claude 4.6 help to implement this

review_comments.body: I think we need to reliably append `flags` after `argv`.
what's with the indentation on these examples?
worst case we could split the `argv` option into the one before vs the one after (read-only) appending flags
i presume under `explicitBool` this would be handled different from omission
maybe unfortunate that this isn't tested so far including in the `snid` example
Tabs maybe?

one remaining question mark for here is commands exposing sub-commands (e.g. `nix` v3 cli), in which case:

- sub-commands would not just not fit the `--flag` pattern
- we might additionally get different flag sets after such sub-commands
- such flags scoped to the selected sub-command may even differ depending on the sub-command used
It can't be tested because it isn't implemented.

yes, look at PR  https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/510698 we have a newer type there. but it still uses mkOrder under the hood, I think mkOrder is the correct surface here to expose to the user, since it what the rest of the module system already uses.

probably the existing service modules should be changed in a separate PR, but having them here makes the changes easier to review. I can draft the PR, so we can keep those changes to showcase the new features and before merging remove the snid changes

review_comments.body: I think we want something like wrappers `package` option which controlls the first element of argv (which is usually the binary to run). Otherwise argv can also be used for positional arguments, which usually come after the flags?
ah right, the documentation is still from an earlier implementation, will fix it tomorrow

Yeah, that looks like a much nicer utility for this. 

I don't think we need to necessarily wait for #510698 to merge. But I guess we should leave a comment to change the impl after it merges.

sub commands would just get different modules, where we would set argv to something like `[ (lib.getExe pkgs.nix) "flake" ]` and then use flags as usual. the main question is probably how multiple modules should be exposed in that case. but since that is not answered yet in this PR it seems a bit out of scope. But it's already good to think about it

env can probably be in another PR, where we can use it to set environment in the systemd service. I don't want to introduce a wrapper yet and changing the systemd implementation would increase the scope of this PR a bit, so removing it is probably the safest option for now

maybe sub-commands by themselves could have their wrappers exposed like `nix = { flake = <wrapper>; };` or something, but then perhaps the top-level thing would similarly need to be a wrapper (routing to the child wrappers?) to handle the parent flags... maybe positional args need more thought, hm.

one thing to note for the environment vars for the wrappers later is that we should have a way of defining if the parent environment gets appended and in which order (like if PATH is inherited and the order)

```suggestion
              types.path
              types.bool
```

We should support paths as will, as these are quite often used as command line arguments, e.g. paths to generated config files.

```suggestion
          - string / path / int: rendered as the option's argument, joined to the
```

See above.
I'm fine with the inclusion

reviews.body: Due to not being implemented, I think the `process.env` and such should either be removed or just turn this PR into a draft until they're implemented. Either way, it isn't ready for merge in its current state

Other than the requested changes, I think the idea of this is pretty good. In practice, the current cleanest method of doing this is with a wrapper. Being able to do this directly would be quite elegant.
left a few comments - i love the idea, tho i think there may still be a few different ways to improve coverage of relevant scenarios (and testing thereof)
Sept the small nitpicks from @vog, LGTM.
